title: Build a portfolio, not just a feed
intro: Start with one real piece of work. Your Sawwiq page brings your projects together so clients can see what you do. A project can contain one image or a group of related images.
nudgeTitle: Not sure what to add first?
nudgeBody: Your profile is you. A client or brand is who the work was for. A portfolio post shows one project or piece of work. We will walk you through an example.
profileStep: Say who you are and choose the services you actually offer.
workStep: Publish one genuine work sample. One image is enough to start.
optionalHelp: A client record, a service package, and connected social accounts are not required to publish your first work sample.

profile.title: Your profile
profile.body: You, your agency or your studio: name, introduction and services.

client.title: Client or brand (optional)
client.body: The business this work was made for. One client can have several projects and social links.

project.title: One portfolio post
project.body: One project or related piece of work, with your role and a short explanation.

images.title: The images inside it
images.body: One to ten related images or screenshots. The first image is the cover.

postTitle: What should go in this post?
postBody: Group work from one project here. Keep a different client or unrelated project in a separate post. This image form accepts 1–10 images or screenshots; it does not accept video files.
clientTitle: A client here is not a login or a connected social account
clientBody: Create one record for the brand or business you worked for, then select it on each related portfolio post. Social links describe that brand; a pasted link does not verify access or authorship. For personal or confidential work, leave the client unselected and describe it without identifying details.
examplesTitle: See an example before you start
examplesNote: Illustrative examples only—not real clients, published work or performance claims. Nothing here is added to your portfolio automatically.

social.label: Social campaign
social.role: My role: photography and post design
social.media: Menu photos + post designs + permitted campaign screenshots belong in this one project.
social.caption: Explain the brief, what you personally delivered and what each image shows. Add results only when you can substantiate them.

identity.label: Brand identity
identity.role: My role: logo and identity design
identity.media: Logo variations + colors + packaging mockups belong together, rather than as unrelated posts.
identity.caption: Describe your part in the identity. Credit collaborators. Clearly label concept or practice work.

photo.label: Photography
photo.media: Select related images from the same shoot. Do not mix different clients to fill the image limit.
photo.caption: Explain the assignment and your role. Do not show people, private briefs or client data without permission.

website.label: Website / app
website.client: Personal project or a permitted client
website.media: Desktop + phone screenshots + selected details from this project.
website.caption: Explain whether you designed, built or contributed to the product. This example does not claim live app embedding is enabled.

tourTitle: Highlight a field in the form

focus.images: Choose 1–10 images for this project. The first is the cover. You do not need ten images.
focus.caption: Explain what was needed, your role and what these images show.
focus.client: Choose the client or brand only when appropriate. Leaving this blank is allowed.
focus.services: Select the services demonstrated by this work—not every service you offer.

structure:
Project or piece of work: [describe it]
My role: [what I personally did]
What is shown: [explain these images]
Result, only if evidenced: [optional; remove when unknown]
structureAdded: An outline was added. Replace the brackets with your own details before publishing.
structurePreserved: Your description was kept unchanged. Clear it yourself to use the blank outline.
formMissing: Open the Add work page to use the field guide.
publishReminder: Check that the images belong together, explain your own role, and share only material you have permission to show. Do not invent results, clients or endorsements.
existingBody: Use your original images, or the existing PDF and Behance import tools when available. Review the grouping, client and description before publishing. Importing and account connection are different actions.
connectionsTitle: Social account connection: what it means
connectionsBody: A public link is not an authorized connection. Google, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok need their own consent-based integrations. Do not share passwords or paste access tokens. Automatic social imports are not enabled by this guide.
